note: The golden corpus for PeTTa's tagged wire codec. Hand-written from the
grammar in CODEC.md, not generated from any implementation, so passing it
is evidence about an implementation rather than a restatement of one.
Every value here was checked against the shipped codecs on 2026-08-20.
A driver implements four operations over one concrete encoding:
read(text)      the engine's reader plus this codec's encoder
roundtrip(wire) decode to the host's own atom, then encode it back
render(wire)    decode, then print with the printer this binding ships
transport(wire) serialise to the concrete encoding and parse it back
Each refuses by raising. Wire terms compare up to a renaming of v
payloads and byte-exactly everywhere else, because a v payload is an
identity within its term and never a display name.
Two escapes, because JSON cannot write what the wire can: {"$float":
"inf"|"-inf"|"nan"} is that float, and {"$host": "opaque"} is a value
only the host can mint, which a driver supplies for itself.

s.means: a symbol: a name that denotes itself

g.means: a grounded value carried as text; a string crosses this way

n.means: a grounded Number or BigInt; signed-i64 width fixes an integer's language type

b.means: a grounded boolean, written True and False in source

v.means: a variable, the payload an identity within this term

e.means: an expression, its children in order; the empty one is unit

o.means: a live host value crossing by reference, in process only

h.payload: registry id, and its printed text outbound
h.means: a native engine value held by reference

u.means: an answer whose truth is undefined under the well-founded semantics

a.payload: theta, residue, k, and optionally a value
a.means: an answer together with the bindings it is returned under

x.payload: end, declined, or error with a term
x.means: stream control: exhaustion, no answer at all, or a failure kept as a value

core.note: What a storage provider must speak. The remote JSON wire is this.

full.note: The in-process host binding: core plus booleans, host references, native handles, and the three frames.

frames_note: The frames are DIRECTIONAL, so a driver decomposes the ones its own
side reads. The engine writes u and the host reads it; the host writes
a and the engine reads it. Nothing shipped decomposes x, so it appears
here only in the refusal that says a stream-control frame is not an
atom; its three items are specified in CODEC.md.

cases.note: A symbol denotes itself. The payload is the name exactly as written, with no sigil and no quoting.
Names are Unicode text. A token ends at whitespace, parenthesis or semicolon and at nothing else, so a letter from any script is an ordinary name character.
A hyphen is a name character, not an operator.
A space name is an ordinary symbol; the ampersand carries no encoding of its own.
A string is a grounded value and not a symbol. The payload holds the text without its quotes; the quotes belong to the text form.
The empty string is a value, distinct from the empty expression.

The payload holds the DECODED text. Five escapes exist in the text form, quote backslash newline tab return, and a printed string stays on one line so every line-oriented consumer re-parses it to itself.
The inclusive lower boundary of Number's integer range. The same n tag carries both integer types, and the exact value recovers which one this is.
The inclusive upper boundary of Number's integer range.
One below signed i64 is BigInt. Reusing n avoids duplicating the type already determined by the exact value.
One above signed i64 is BigInt. A codec must carry every digit or refuse the payload.

Two to the fifty-three plus one is still Number because it fits signed i64, but it is the smallest integer a binary64 cannot hold. A codec that can hold this MUST hold it and one that cannot MUST refuse it; see refuse-integer-beyond-exact-range.
Past sixty-four bits, so this atom has type BigInt. SWI's integer values are unbounded and the tag carries the value, never a rounding of it.

A float whose value is a whole number is still a float. !(== 1.0 1) answers False, so a transport with one number type must carry the distinction some other way or refuse the value; conflating them returns a different atom, the same failure the exactness rule forbids for wide integers.

The engine prints the arbiter's layout (LeaTTa RyuLean4/Runtime.lean:371-396: positional while the value has at most sixteen digits before the point), and Python's repr shares both the digits and this threshold, so the two shipped printers agree here where they used to split 1.0e+10 against 10000000000.0. Gnd's own renderer implements the same law, so the two printers agree everywhere a float prints. Pinned so a change to either printer is visible.
The other end of the range, agreeing the same way: the engine's arbiter layout drops the mantissa's redundant .0 exactly where repr does.

The arbiter's spelling, which is hyperon's f64 Display. It prints and it does not read back: `inf` reads as the SYMBOL inf, MeTTa having no literal for a non-finite number, so this case has no text and the seam refuses the whole class rather than storing something that comes back different.

Both printers spell it the arbiter's way now, one authority for one atom. Comparing two decodings of it is the one place equality is not enough, since a NaN is not equal to itself; the wire carries THE non-finite value and two readings of it are the same term.
The language spells its booleans True and False; the payload is the lowercase text. The two spellings are not a drift: the payload names the value, the text form names the constant.

The reader maps both spellings onto the one constant, so lowercase source READS as the boolean and WRITES back capitalised. The term round-trips; the text does not, which is the one place the two forms are not inverse.

The reader that keeps names writes the source name. The engine's own printer numbers variables by first occurrence, because an engine variable carries no name; a binding that keeps its atoms in the host prints the name it read.
Unit. An expression with no children, not a missing value and not the empty string.
Depth is data. A decoder must not meet its host's recursion ceiling on it; see expression-deep.
One expression holding a child of every core kind plus a boolean.
One name is one variable. Two occurrences of a payload are two occurrences of the same cell, which is what makes the payload an identity.
Two names are two variables, so the renaming that compares two wire terms is a bijection and never collapses these onto the repeated case.
An equation is an ordinary expression headed by =; nothing about a definition is special on the wire.

The one reserved payload. `_` is fresh at every occurrence and never shares, exactly as $_ does in source, so two of them constrain nothing and the wire is NOT an identity here. A codec that decodes into a host's own variables resolves it and gives two distinct ones back; a codec that carries wire terms to a store keeps the payload. No encoder ever writes it: reading $_ mints an identity instead, which is why this case has no text.

The wire is strictly more expressive than the text form. A name holding whitespace prints, and the printed text reads back as two forms rather than one, so it has no text spelling. The same holds for a name that reads as a number, a variable, a string or a boolean: 42, $x, True, a"b and a;b are all encodable and none round-trips through text.

A live host value crossing by reference, not by serialisation: the same object comes back, so identity, mutation and accessors all see one thing. Only an in-process encoding can carry it, which is why it is outside the core profile.
Four hundred deep. A recursive decoder in a host with a shallow stack fails here and nowhere else in this corpus, which is the point of the case.

refusals.because: z names no tag, and the tag set is closed
a wire term is a tagged array and never a bare value
a wire term carries a tag
every term tag takes exactly one payload
every term tag takes exactly one payload; the three-element form belongs to h alone
a tag is a claim about its payload: s carries text
s carries text, and an array is not text however it prints
g carries text; a number belongs under n
g carries text, not an arbitrary structure. A codec that admits one stores a value no other codec can read back.
n carries a number. The engine has rationals and the wire has no spelling for one, so a rational is refused here rather than carried as its text.
n carries a number; a boolean belongs under b
v carries the identity as text
b carries exactly true or false. Reading anything else as false answers a question nobody asked.
b carries exactly true or false; truthiness is not the rule here
e carries an array of wire terms
e carries an array of wire terms
a malformed child makes the whole term malformed; nothing decodes partially
an answer frame is not an atom, and the position asked for an atom
a stream-control frame is not an atom
a transport whose numbers are binary64 rounds this, and a store that rounds an atom answers a different atom. Refuse the payload; never round it.
JSON has no literal for a non-finite number. An in-process encoding carries one; a JSON one refuses it rather than inventing a spelling.

frames.note: An answer as bindings for the query's variables. residue true means the provider discharged the whole goal; k null means the degenerate annotation, semiring one.
A ground answer binds nothing and is still an answer, distinct from no answer at all.

The candidate-with-bindings reading: the answer atom together with the bindings it is returned under. The value must unify with the pattern under theta, and an answer whose value contradicts its theta drops.

The part of the goal the provider did not discharge. It decodes against theta's own name table, so its variables ARE the query's, and the engine evaluates it: a result that is not false contributes one closure and false drops the answer.
An answer whose truth is undefined under the well-founded semantics: the value, and the delay condition it hangs on. Never nested inside an expression; it wraps a whole answer.

transcripts.note: One group per ! directive, holding that directive's answers in order.
Arithmetic remains exact in SWI and the result becomes BigInt when it leaves signed i64.
A comparison answers the boolean tag, not the symbol False.
Three answers in one group. The group is the directive, not the answer.
An empty group is a directive that answered nothing, which is not the same as a directive that answered ().
A one-element expression holding a string, so the g tag reaches a transcript.
A definition contributes no group; only ! directives do.
